register.title: Evan Daniel's n154 certificate at 1d2bb82, issue694
register.headline: Daniel's smaller n154 packing, a new KKT point in Couzo's #586 family, certified exactly
register.source_checks: The author reports that his two exact rational checkers, verify_cert.py (separating axes) and verify_cert2.py (polygon intersection), accept the certificate and its regularized view at the same side. The source reports a KKT point that it has not shown to be a strict local minimum (its second-order test is inconclusive), 58 corner-corner contacts with no corner-corner MILP descent, 9 rattlers and 38 tilted squares, and calls it a different KKT point from #586's in the same family: the matched contact graphs share 232 pairs, 61 are only here and 64 only in #586's, and a morph walk finds no path between the two up to 1e-2 above #586's side. Those are numerical evidence at 80 digits and a heuristic, as the source says, not proofs. No source program ran here.
register.credit: Credit Evan Daniel (https://github.com/evand/square-packing), whose chained explorer removed two squares from the register's s(156) packing (Daniil Ostashev's) and, with crossovers against close relatives of Francisco Couzo's #586 packing, and a later restart of his basin explorer, reached this packing; the issue asks that #586's arrangement (itself continued from Daniel's #552) and Ostashev's s(156) packing be credited as its starts. The search, the checks and the request were done with Claude (Claude Code) under Evan Daniel's direction.
register.next_rung: Independently review the retained replay, then adopt at 154.

bibliography.note: One complete exact certificate at 1d2bb82035af4b7eb4658488543e46b67d1099ca, s(154) <= 1615137617595210068732072760947/(125*10^27), found by the author's chained and basin explorers from Ostashev's s(156) packing, crossed with relatives of Couzo's #586 packing; the issue asks that #586's arrangement and the s(156) packing be credited as its starts, and calls it a different KKT point from #586's in its family. A same-side regularized view and the source's comparison with #586 are retained beside it. MIT-licensed; Claude assistance disclosed. KKT statements are the author's numerical evidence; the source does not claim a strict local minimum, and no local or global optimality claim is made.
